newsitem.title: USA: Core Industries valve unit key to talks - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Core Industries valve unit key to talks - analysts.

text.p: Core Industries Inc, in talks about the possible sale of the firm, was most likely approached by a buyer who is most interested in its Fluid Controls valve business, analysts said.
"I would suspect the fluid control (business) is what is behind this," Ingalls & Snyder analyst Alexander Blanton said of Core Industries' announcement. "It's a high margin business."
Blanton said he believed Core Industries' high-margin valve business could attract a buyer given the recent consolidation in this segment of the capital goods industry.
For example, Tyco International Ltd in May said it would acquire Keystone International Inc, which makes industrial valves. In addition, ITT Industries Inc recently acquired Goulds Pumps Inc.

Core Industries said Monday it was in discussions with an unnamed third party related to the possible sale of the company. A spokesman declined to say if the company had sought a bid or received an unsolicited offer.

Roney & Co analyst Dean Gulis, who had no direct knowledge of the discussions, said a buyer would most likely be interested in Core Industries' valve business, which is part of its Fluid Controls and Construction Products Segment.
He believed that Core Industries most likely was approached by an interested party and had not put itself on the block for sale.
"I do not think that the company has been actively seeking a buyer," Gulis said.

Gulis added that a buyer might also be interested in Core Industries' electronic instrument business, which is part of its Test, Measurement and Control segment. Core Industries' other segment makes farm equipment.
Blanton added that the valve business could be especially attractive if the continued growth of the U.S. economy leads to expansion of plant capacity in process industries.
He said Core Industries' announcement came as little surprise given the recent rise in the stock. Shares after the announcement rose 3-3/4 to 23-1/2 and closed the day at 23-1/4, up 3-1/2.
In addition, Core Industries reported stronger than expected earnings for the third quarter ended May 31 of $0.44 a share, up from $0.34 a year ago.
